title: Apartment or landed? Start with the life you want.
excerpt: Sean revisits a familiar debate through land scarcity, changing priorities and the purpose of a home.
takeaways: The two formats emerge in different development conditions.
Income and life priorities affect housing preferences.
Safety and security remain central to a home.

sections.heading: A comparison with context
paragraphs: Sean's episode notes frame the apartment-versus-landed debate around development conditions. High-rise homes tend to appear as land becomes scarce, so comparing the formats also means considering the setting in which they are built.

sections.heading: Preferences change with circumstances
paragraphs: The notes raise an argument about a possible ceiling on non-landed resale prices as the income needed to buy increases and buyers' priorities shift. This is a discussion point from the episode, not a verified rule for every apartment market.

sections.heading: Return to the purpose of the home
paragraphs: Sean identifies safety and security as a fundamental priority. The discussion therefore extends beyond choosing a housing label to what a home should provide.

closing: As a reading prompt, write down the three things your home needs to do for you before comparing formats. This prompt is editorial, not a quotation from Sean.
sourceNote: Based on the original video's published episode notes. Full captions were unavailable; the summary covers those notes rather than the complete conversation.
